binding.request_0: a -> b; terminal notice returns to a
binding.request_1_and_2: b -> a; terminal notices share b FIFO
binding.capacity: In retiring-notice-reserves-capacity, barrier-reserves-capacity, fence-waits-for-current-execution and fifo-admission-cannot-overtake: the host's work queue (worker_jobs). Each step is followed by the worker's DiscoverWork; admit(i) is the worker's ClaimWork, which must give request i's delivery job, and complete(i) ends that job. A refused admit(i) is ClaimWork giving older work: a notification to retire, a closing request's work, or a request ahead in the admission queue. A fence waits for the effect transaction open in its store. Local callback execution is not physical VMM occupancy; VM slots and the host's admission locks are outside this replay.
binding.initial_environment: Two seeded agents/mandates/current SQL placements; real accounts/tokens and encrypted Transit. Private-schema attempt_limit default is 2.
binding.time: Model deadlines and lease expiration age the corresponding SQL timestamps; production guards and commits still execute.
binding.complete: Real local SQLite writer commits, production request ACK then authenticated VM-bound encrypted reply transaction.
binding.observe: Authenticated production owner Request lookup returns terminal state and, for success, decrypted private result. Observation flag records a successful read, not a new persisted Go state.
binding.recycle: Only model-slot binding is released. Old request UUIDs, results, notification reception and SQLite effects must remain; next arrival allocates a fresh UUID. A refused recycle (notice outstanding) is checked against the production purge (Transit.PurgeExpired, seven days aged): the delivered request's content goes, the reply the pending notice carries stays, and its owner still reads it.
binding.notification_failure: Actual TCP ECONNREFUSED after SQL dispatch authorization; lease expiry permits retry. Final retirement uses production event fence and rejects delayed copies.
binding.store_availability: Stop/drain real local mTLS server and close SQLite; actual Health/Fence failures mark it unavailable. Recovery reopens the same current SQLite file with authenticated local transport. This is not rollback restore or a VMM reboot.
binding.authority_availability: The production owner lookup has its own real PostgreSQL pool through a loopback proxy. Closing listener and active connections causes actual lookup failure; reopening the endpoint restores lookup of the same encrypted outcome. This is read-path SQL authority availability, not D5 independent key-root recovery.
binding.worker_availability: A dedicated Go subprocess executes DiscoverWork, ClaimWork, ClaimDelivery, AuthorizeDispatch, encrypted resolution, delivery ACK/CompleteWork and private reply transactions. SIGKILL is observed after request acceptance/discovery; a fresh process consumes the retained ticket. mTLS/SQLite callback driving remains in the parent. This is not the full Firecracker worker service.
binding.deletion: Only in deleted-destination-rejects-new-work, with no request in flight: requestDelete is the owner's production deletion request for agent a (store 0), finishDelete the production fence of agent/a in both local stores, their SQL receipts and the tombstone commit. Pending is agent a QUIESCING, complete is DELETING or DELETED. The refused arrival is a production submission from a's still-running VM, refused for its placement.

remaining_case_requirements.retiring-notice-waits-for-capacity: Not replayable as Go stands: request 1 (b -> a) arrives after notice 0 (to a), and a's mailbox, FIFO over requests and notices, refuses admit(1). With a third agent executing request 1, Go would not refuse the retirement: a notification attempt and a barrier both take the host's exclusive turn behind a synchronous callback, and neither waits for an asynchronous computation. P3 lets the attempts through and holds the barrier.
remaining_case_requirements.delete-running-agent-preserves-other-wor: Three agents (request 1 executed by c) and a deletion that closes request 0 at its tombstone, not by its own closure: TestDeletionOfARunningAgentPreservesOtherWork, outside this replay
